mainEntity.name: Sam Miller
mainEntity.description: Application Security Analyst based in Atlanta. I write Python, work with GraphQL and REST APIs, organize security data, build security data pipelines, automate exception follow-up and SBOM collection, interpret security findings, and partner with developers on remediation. I earned a B.B.A. in Information Security & Assurance from Kennesaw State University, graduating Magna Cum Laude, and took part in the USG Goes Global (USGG) study abroad experience in London in June and July 2024.

hasCredential.name: B.B.A. in Information Security & Assurance, Magna Cum Laude

subjectOf.name: Smart VIN Decoder
subjectOf.description: Solo Information Systems semester project: Python command-line client for the NHTSA API, with basic VIN input checks, JSON response parsing, and in-memory lookup history for the session.

subjectOf.name: DNS Sinkhole
subjectOf.description: Home lab: Pi-hole configured on a Raspberry Pi for DNS filtering and visibility into query and blocking activity.

subjectOf.name: Server Security Capstone
subjectOf.description: Bachelor's capstone using Nmap and Greenbone to discover exposed services and assess a lab server, with researched findings, hardening recommendations, an executive summary, and scan evidence.

subjectOf.name: Incident Response Plan Capstone
subjectOf.description: Bachelor's capstone: a semester-long team project led by Sam Miller to develop an incident response plan for a fictional organization, coordinating early response leadership and communications. The plan organizes playbooks, severity levels, communications, and responsibilities, with revisions after a rehearsal and team review.

subjectOf.name: Build useful security data pipelines
subjectOf.description: I collect repository and finding data through APIs, organize it into consistent records, and build repeatable reporting workflows. Gives engineering and leadership a clearer view of the data they need to review.

subjectOf.name: Keep exceptions connected to findings
subjectOf.description: I built scheduled workflows to track approved exceptions, match them to findings, and revisit them when the approval expires. Keeps exception follow-up connected to the current state of a finding.

subjectOf.name: Make security reports easier to query
subjectOf.description: I built Python tools for looking up security-report data, checking incoming files, and reviewing upcoming exception dates. Makes recurring questions easier to answer without repeatedly downloading whole reports.

subjectOf.name: Investigate findings and scanner behavior
subjectOf.description: I configure scanners, investigate false positives and unexpected finding-state changes, and work with developers on remediation. Helps distinguish a code issue from a scan or policy issue before deciding what to do next.

subjectOf.name: Organize dependency evidence
subjectOf.description: I built scheduled API workflows to collect CycloneDX software bills of materials and organize dependency snapshots for review. Keeps dependency information available beyond an individual pipeline run.

subjectOf.name: Make security tools easier to adopt
subjectOf.description: I supported the move from Snyk to GitLab with integration checks, reporting, automation, and walkthroughs for embedded engineers. Helps engineers understand the new tools and what changed in their workflow.
